newsitem.title: CHINA: Forty pct of small-medium China breweries in red.
newsitem.headline: Forty pct of small-medium China breweries in red.

text.p: About 40 percent of China's medium and small-sized breweries are losing money due to small production scales and fierce competition, the Economic Information Daily said on Monday.
China now has more than 800 breweries and domestic beer production has increased at an average of 25 percent a year over the past ten years, the newspaper said.

Beer makers have sprung up all over the country amid rising demand, but competition among domestic brewers and the growing popularity of foreign brands meant many producers were now suffering losses, it said.
Most Chinese beers are local brands produced by small-scale breweries, with only a few brands available nationwide.
China's biggest and most famous beer producer, Tsingtao Brewery Co Ltd, had only a 2.3 percent share of the domestic market, the newspaper said.

Some 30 large and medium-sized state-run or collectively-owned brewers had set up ventures with foreign companies since 1992 because the lacked funds for technical renovation, it said but gave no further details.
